guide.title: Malthael's Overview
guide.text:
Malthael is a Bruiser who naturally counters high-Health Heroes.
Calm players who are able to apply Reaper's Mark onto
multiple targets will be rewarded with overwhelming sustain damage and great
survivability.

guide.title: Malthael's Strengths and Weaknesses
guide.text:
Strengths
Excellent self-sustain
Powerful duelist
Solid non-Structural PvE damage
Very difficult to escape from once marked by Reaper's Mark
Last Rites is excellent to execute Heroes
Multiple sources of percent-based damage that cannot be reduced by Armor
Weaknesses
Highly prone to being kited
Offers limited utility beyond raw damage
Limited upfront burst damage
Weak siege damage
Low maximum Health, being vulnerable to crowd control and bursts during the early game

guide.title: Malthael's Synergies and Counters
guide.text:
Malthael synergizes with
Heroes that displace enemies, like Garrosh and E.T.C. are excellent
with Malthael, as they will ease the focus on a target, allowing Last Rites
to execute it. One of Malthael's problems is that he takes
too long to reduce an enemy's health to Last Rites's threshold,
so he is great with Greymane's Cursed Bullet or
with Tychus's The Bigger They Are....
Due to how Malthael's damage and self sustain is completely
tied to Soul Rip, he has excellent synergy with Heroes that
can reduce his Cooldowns. While Ana with Nano Boost
turns Malthael into an immortal killing machine, Malfurion can enhance
his effectiveness very often through Innervate.
Malthael is countered by
As a Bruiser with a rather telegraphed play style, Malthael
is very vulnerable to any form of targeted crowd control. Furthermore,
since his main gap closer, Wraith Strike, requires him to
either attack or hit a slow skillshot, he is naturally bound to
be kited by nimble ranged Heroes.
Against experienced players, Blaze will be an excellent counter
to Malthael. Bunker Drop
cleanses Reaper's Mark
from anyone that enters it. It also denies Last Rites's damage.
Considering enemies will be inside bunker, Malthael's self-sustain will be very limited, as
Malthael will not be able to use Soul Rip
to sustain himself.

guide.title: Malthael's Maps
guide.text:
Malthael's stronger maps
Malthael's average maps
Malthael's weaker maps
Malthael is a very versatile Hero that is excellent in many different maps.
On a Pale Horse enhances Malthael's effectiveness in
large maps, while his outstanding double soak makes
him a good pick on Infernal Shrines, Sky Temple, and
Towers of Doom. His good dueling capabilities can be abused
on Dragon Shire and Tomb of the Spider Queen. Additionally,
since Malthael can easily capture Mercenary Camps, due to his good self-sustain,
he is good on macro-heavy maps, like Garden of Terror
and Blackheart's Bay.
Malthael cannot abuse his fast rotation and waveclear
in 2-lane maps. Therefore, we do not recommend him on Hanamura Temple and
Battlefield of Eternity.

guide.title: Malthael's Tips and Tricks
guide.text:
Malthael's Basic Attacks hit enemies in a 180 degree arc; use this to maintain Reaper's Mark on as many targets as possible.
Reaper's Mark's damage also works against most non-Structure units, making it effective against Bosses and Map Objectives.
You can hold the default Q hotkey to repeatedly cast Soul Rip without effort.
Wraith Strike is useful for quickly avoiding impending skillshots and areas of effect.
Tormented Souls resets Wraith Strike's Cooldown on-use AND when Tormented Souls ends.
A skull marker appears above Heroes that would die to Last Rites's damage.
Do not be conservative with Last Rites, as it is better to guarantee a kill and get the Cooldown reduction than to hold it.
Inevitable End can be used to bait important Abilities from the enemy team, as the Cooldown is relatively low.
Due to Shroud of Wisdom's delay, it should be activated around 1.5 seconds before going in, as most Abilities will be used on you in the first seconds. Using it too quickly might result in having reduced uptime, while taking too long might cost your life.
See our Abilities page for further information »

guide.title: Malthael's Role in the Current Meta
guide.text:
As a strong duelist with outstanding self-sustain and good
waveclear, Malthael makes for a strong Offlaner, though he can
also dispatch Mercenary Camps with ease.
Reaper's Mark defines Malthael as a premiere
counterpick to team compositions
that are melee-heavy or otherwise feature Heroes with large Health pools. This
Trait also allows Malthael to deal a significant amount of damage to Bosses and
Monsters from Objectives. In general however, he tends to do
poorly against ranged Heroes, and should not be picked if enemies can easily kite you.
Malthael's macro playstyle consists on constantly clearing waves
while damaging the opposing Offlaner through
Reaper's Mark and Soul Rip.
At fights, we recommend to poke
the enemy frontline with Death Shroud
and Soul Rip until the opposing team wastes important Abilities.
If you try to engage by yourself, enemies will easily
burst you down, because of Malthael's low maximum Health. For this reason,
it is better to be patient until a good opportunity shows up.

abilities.title: Malthael's Tips and Tricks
abilities.text:
Malthael's Basic Attacks hit enemies in a 180 degree arc; use this to maintain Reaper's Mark on as many targets as possible.
Reaper's Mark's damage also works against most non-Structure units, making it effective against Bosses and Map Objectives.
You can hold the default Q hotkey to repeatedly cast Soul Rip without effort.
Wraith Strike is useful for quickly avoiding impending skillshots and areas of effect.
Tormented Souls resets Wraith Strike's Cooldown on-use AND when Tormented Souls ends.
A skull marker appears above Heroes that would die to Last Rites's damage.
Do not be conservative with Last Rites, as it is better to guarantee a kill and get the Cooldown reduction than to hold it.
Inevitable End can be used to bait important Abilities from the enemy team, as the Cooldown is relatively low.
Due to Shroud of Wisdom's delay, it should be activated around 1.5 seconds before going in, as most Abilities will be used on you in the first seconds. Using it too quickly might result in having reduced uptime, while taking too long might cost your life.

abilities.title: A Note on Malthael's Basic Attack
abilities.text:
Malthael's Basic Attacks have a unique feature: instead of hitting a single
target like most other Basic Attacks, they hits all enemies in a 180-degree arc
centered on their target. This attribute is particularly useful for claiming
Mercenary Camps and waveclearing purposes, especially since
Reaper's Mark, which will be discussed below, is inflicted to all targets damaged
by these Basic Attacks. Since Malthael's power is directly dependent on how
many targets are affected by Reaper's Mark, making the most of this area of
effect feature is essential to thriving.

abilities.title: Reaper's Mark
abilities.text:
Reaper's Mark
(D)
Malthael
Passive
Basic Attacks cleave in an area in front of Malthael and afflict non-Structure targets with Reaper's Mark for 4 seconds. Marked enemies are revealed and take damage equal to 2% of their maximum Health every 1 second.
Although we typically list Hero Abilities in their in-game order, Malthael's
Trait is quite unique in that it impacts the rest of his Abilities. It is thus
listed first, so as to provide a clearer context for everything else.
Reaper's Mark is core to Malthael
as his key Abilities— Soul Rip
and Wraith Strike—can only be used against targets that have
been affected by Reaper's Mark. It is as such vital that you not only master the
art of applying Reaper's Mark through Basic Attacks by seizing any occasion to
do so, but also, see to apply the Trait to as many different targets as possible
by trying to hit as many enemies as possible through Malthael's cleaving Basic
Attacks and Death Shroud.
By nature, this Trait makes Malthael's Basic Attacks deal some of the highest
damage on a per-hit basis, the caveat being that this damage is dealt over time.
Hitting the same target twice merely refreshes Reaper's Mark to its 4-second
duration rather than stacking the damage-over-time effect.
It should be noted that Reaper's Mark also functions against Bosses and
Monsters from Objectives, making Malthael exceptional at
dealing with such matter.

abilities.title: Soul Rip
abilities.text:
Soul Rip
(Q)
Malthael
Mana: 25
Cooldown: 2 seconds
Extract the souls of nearby enemies afflicted by Reaper's Mark, dealing 100 (+4% per level) damage and healing Malthael for 25 (+4% per level) per target hit. Heroic targets heal Malthael for an additional 4% of the Hero's maximum Health.
Soul Rip provides Malthael with a reasonable amount of area of effect damage. The
Ability's main point of appeal, however, is its healing effect, which is based
off any Hero hit's maximum Health. This makes Malthael strive in situations
where multiple Heroes have been hit by Reaper's Mark, as the effects of
Soul Rip stack fully per target hit. Under certain circumstances, the Ability
thus allows Malthael to be surprisingly difficult to kill, and is the second
reason, beyond Reaper's Mark, why Malthael does so well against high-Health
Heroes.
While laning or claiming Mercenary Camps, Soul Rip plays an important part
in Malthael's self sustain. Death Shroud can and should
be used to apply Reaper's Mark to as many Minions or Mercenaries as possible so
that Soul Rip's healing effects can trigger against as many targets as possible.
This interaction is key to Malthael's strong presence as a offlane.
Note that you can simply hold [Q] to effortlessly cast Soul
Rip without having to repeatedly press its cast key.

abilities.title: Wraith Strike
abilities.text:
Wraith Strike
(W)
Malthael
Mana: 30
Cooldown: 5 seconds
Instantly teleport through an enemy afflicted by Reaper's Mark, dealing 59 (+4% per level) damage and refreshing Reaper's Mark.
Wraith Strike provides Malthael with outstanding combat mobility which, in
turn, translates into high uptime. Combined with the large
sustained damage provided by Reaper's Mark and Soul Rip,
Malthael becomes one of the most dangerous Heroes to pressure both Tanks
and non-Tanks, and particularly when defensive Abilities have been expended.
Since Wraith Strike teleports Malthael behind his target, it can be used to
reliably body block escaping or chasing foes
as well as to free yourself from enemy body block while being ganked. Its
instantaneous cast speed also makes it useful for dodging impending delayed
Abilities, such as Jaina's Blizzard, and becomes a key part in Malthael's
general survival. Its short cooldown means it can be used very liberally,
granted it is safe to do so.
For escaping purposes, Death Shroud can be used to apply
Reaper's Mark to a far target, upon which Wraith Strike can then be used.
It should be noted that Wraith Strike places Malthael's
Basic Attack on a cooldown. So, for damage-per-second purposes, it is better to use
a Basic Attack right before using Wraith Strike, in order to not lose possible damage (only if
you are in melee range with the target).

abilities.title: Death Shroud
abilities.text:
Death Shroud
(E)
Malthael
Mana: 50
Cooldown: 8 seconds
After 0.25 seconds, unleash a wave of dark mist that applies Reaper's Mark to enemies it hits.
Death Shroud fulfills the double function of allowing Malthael to
apply Reaper's Mark from range and in an area of effect. Although
Death Shroud does no damage by default, the mark it applies deals some by
nature. Without Death Shroud, it can be very difficult for Malthael to safely
engage against ranged Heroes, let alone catch up to them. As such, mastering
the skillshot-like Ability is key to playing Malthael successfully. Its
slow speed means that you will have to either predict where your intended
target will be moving to, or rely on crowd control provided by
allies to hit Death Shroud.
Death Shroud's ability to apply Reaper's Mark in an area makes it his most
reliable way of benefiting from Soul Rip's healing against as
many targets as possible. When unthreatened by ranged damage,
Malthael's Basic Attacks should be used to spread Reaper's Mark so as to
conserve Mana.

abilities.title: Tormented Souls
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Tormented Souls
(R)
Malthael
Heroic
Mana: 20
Cooldown: 60 seconds
Unleash a torrent of souls, continually applying Reaper's Mark to nearby enemies for 4 seconds.
Tormented Souls resets the cooldown of Wraith Strike when activated, and while active, Wraith Strike costs no Mana its cooldown is reduced to 2 seconds.
Tormented Souls has two main purposes. First, it allows Malthael to reliably
apply Reaper's Mark in a large area. Combined with Soul Rip,
this effect makes Malthael particularly threatening and difficult to kill in
team fighting situations. This wide Reaper's Mark application also provides
Malthael with many opportunities to use Wraith Strike offensively
and defensively.
Tormented Souls also completely resets the cooldown of Wraith Strike upon
use and then once again 4 seconds later. This lets you use a first Wraith Strike
aggressively, knowing that the Ability will be available shortly after to
provide you with an opportunity to escape.

abilities.title: Last Rites
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Last Rites
(R)
Malthael
Heroic
Mana: 100
Cooldown: 70 seconds
Apply a death sentence to an enemy Hero that, after 2 seconds, deals damage equal to 50% of their missing Health.
Quest: Enemies killed between the application of Last Rites and within 1.5 seconds of it dealing damage permanently reduce its cooldown by 5 seconds, to a minimum of 20 seconds.
Last Rites's power lies in its ability to reliably deal some
of the game's highest burst damage from range. By nature, Last Rites will kill
any Hero at or below 33% of its maximum Health. This threshold is
indicated by a skull icon floating above nearby enemy Heroes. It should be noted
that even if the target does not die from Last Rites' effect, it is still
damaged. Still, since Last Rites' damage scales with how proportionally low its
target's Health is, the Ability should almost exclusively be used as a finisher.
Certain effects, such as Invulnerability or Stasis effects, can prevent
Last Rites from dealing its damage, although Armor and other forms of
damage mitigation will not. It is important to account for the aforementioned
effects when using Last Rites, especially due to its delayed effect.
Another noteworthy point lies in Last Rites' cooldown reduction clause:
every target who dies while under Last Rites' effect permanently reduces the
Ability's cooldown by 5 seconds. This bonus is acquired whether or not Last
Rites is the source of the killing blow, as long as the dying Hero was under the
effects of Last Rites.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Death's Reach significantly improves Malthael's effective threat range, and is often
picked alongside other Wraith Strike Talents. It is good
against many marksmen, while Fear the Reaper
is better to kite Melee Heroes.
On a Pale Horse provides no combat benefits.
Still, the Talent is excellent if you need to double soak
on relatively big Maps, such as Infernal Shrines, Towers of Doom,
Garden of Terror, Sky Temple, or Cursed Hollow.
Fear the Reaper provides Malthael with utility he sorely lacks:
an on-demand means of improving his mobility. Fear the Reaper is particularly
useful for its underrated ability to remove Malthael's collision, allowing
him to move back to safety unhindered after using Wraith Strike,
without the possibility for enemy Heroes to bodyblock him.
The collision removal is also deceptively useful for dodging Abilities by
allowing you to unpredictably move right through your target.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Die Alone increases Malthael's single-target damage output to very
reasonable amounts, allowing him to duel Heroes he would otherwise not be able
to, such as Thrall. It should be noted that Die Alone can also be used in team
fights by focusing your Reaper's Mark on a single target, though this is
seldom recommended unless you absolutely need to dispatch a specific target. Die
Alone is powerful when solo-laning.
Throwing Shade improves Malthael's ability to poke on
top of increasing his threat range. Throwing Shade is often picked along
Massacre, as your playstyle will be to constantly mark all
possible targets with Reaper's Mark. This Talent is excellent
on Battlefield of Eternity, as it enables good long-ranged poke
against the Immortal.
Black Harvest significantly improves Malthael's area of effect damage over
time output by increasing the duration of Reaper's Mark. This duration
increase also indirectly improves Malthael's survivability and mobility by
making it easier to maintain Reaper's Mark up on multiple targets for
Soul Rip and Wraith Strike purposes. Black Harvest
tends to be picked over Die Alone when the opposing team composition features
2 or more Tanks or other Heroes with high max Health such as Azmodan,
and if you plan to not solo lane.

talent_pages.text:
Cold Hand improves Malthael's ability to stick to his targets by providing

Massacre is excellent to apply Reaper's Mark

It also has good synergy with Mortality, as it will apply
the percent-based damage on all targets.
Touch of Death excels against Heroes with high
self sustain, like Diablo, Dehaka, or Sonya.
It is also a good Talent to counter double-Healer
team compositions and generally impair high burst Healers
such as Whitemane, Rehgar, or Alexstrasza.

Apply a death sentence to an enemy Hero that, after 2 seconds, deals damage equal to 50% of their missing Health.
Quest: Enemies killed between the application of Last Rites and within 1.5 seconds of it dealing damage permanently reduce its cooldown by 5 seconds, to a minimum of 20 seconds.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
In this section we discuss when and why to pick a given Heroic Ability.
If you want to read how they work in detail and/or you are looking for some tips on how to use them,
check them out on the Abilities and Strategy page.
Tormented Souls has two main purposes. First, it allows Malthael to reliably
apply Reaper's Mark in a large area. Combined with Soul Rip,
this effect makes Malthael particularly threatening and difficult to kill in
team fighting situations. This wide Reaper's Mark application also provides
Malthael with many opportunities to use Wraith Strike offensively
and defensively.
Tormented Souls also completely resets the cooldown of Wraith Strike upon
use and then once again 4 seconds later. This lets you use a first Wraith Strike
aggressively, knowing that the Ability will be available shortly after to
provide you with an opportunity to escape. This makes Tormented Souls synergise
particularly well with Mortality and Massacre,
which may be used to quickly damage multiple targets for up to 24% of their total Health.
Last Rites's power lies in its ability to reliably deal some
of the game's highest burst damage from range. By nature, Last Rites will kill
any Hero at or below 33% of its maximum Health. This threshold is
indicated by a skull icon floating above nearby enemy Heroes. It should be noted
that even if the target does not die from Last Rites' effect, it is still
damaged. Still, since Last Rites' damage scales with how proportionally low its
target's Health is, the Ability should almost exclusively be used as a finisher.
Certain effects, such as Invulnerability or Stasis effects, can prevent
Last Rites from dealing its damage, although Armor and other forms of
damage mitigation will not. It is important to account for the aforementioned
effects when using Last Rites, especially due to its delayed effect.
Another noteworthy point lies in Last Rites' cooldown reduction clause:
every target who dies while under Last Rites' effect permanently reduces the
Ability's cooldown by 5 seconds. This bonus is acquired whether or not Last
Rites is the source of the killing blow, as long as the dying Hero was under the
effects of Last Rites.

talent_pages.title: Level 13 Talents for Malthael
talent_pages.text:
✘︎
Soul Siphon
(Level 13)
Malthael
Increase Soul Rip's bonus healing from Heroes to 4.75% of the Hero's maximum Health.
?
Ethereal Existence
(Level 13)
Malthael
Gain 10 Physical Armor per enemy Hero afflicted by Reaper's Mark, up to a maximum of 30.
✓
Inevitable End
(Level 13)
Malthael
Cooldown: 20 seconds
Activate to become Unstoppable for 2 seconds, but remove all active Reaper's Marks.
?
Shroud of Wisdom
(Level 13)
Malthael
Cooldown: 20 seconds
After 2 seconds, gain 50 Spell Armor for 4 seconds.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Soul Siphon's extra healing is not good enough to compare it with
Shroud of Wisdom and Ethereal Existence.
The Healing added by it will not be more efficient than the damage mitigated by
Soul Siphon's counterparts.
Ethereal Existence is used to counter team compositions that rely heavily
on Basic Attacks, and specific Heroes such as Greymane, Raynor
or Illidan.
Inevitable End is one of the most reliable sources of
Unstoppable in the game, as it only has a 20-second cooldown. This Talent excels
against premeditated crowd control, like Diablo's
Apocalypse or Anub'arak's engages. However, it is
also great if the opposing team has ways to disrupt Malthael during the fights, as
Inevitable End will protect him against
these Stuns and Silences.
Be aware that Inevitable End removes all applied marks.
It is better to either activate it after blinking with Wraith Strike,
before using Death Shroud, or during Tormented Souls.
Shroud of Wisdom is used to improve your survivability against
Ability-damage heavy team compositions, featuring burst Heroes such as Jaina,
Li-Ming, or Kael'thas. It should be noted that unlike similar Talents,
Shroud of Wisdom has to be activated two seconds before the Spell Armor
is needed; as such, you need to be wise, as the Talent's name implies, and
predict impending damage burst. Generally, it is safe to assume retaliation
after engaging through Wraith Strike.

talent_pages.title: Level 16 Talents for Malthael
talent_pages.text:
?
Soul Collector
(Level 16)
Malthael
Reduce Soul Rip's cooldown by 0.5 seconds and increase its range by 25%.
✓
Mortality
(Level 16)
Malthael
When damaging a Hero, Wraith Strike deals bonus damage equal to 8% of the Hero's maximum Health.
✘︎
Memento Mori
(Level 16)
Malthael
Reaper's Mark deals 60% increased damage after afflicting an enemy for more than 4 seconds.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Soul Collector significantly improves Malthael's area of effect damage output
and self-sustain, and particularly when picked along other
Talents which improve Soul Rip. If you have been struggling with
team fight survival, Soul Collector should help.
Mortality improves Malthael's
burst damage output, particularly against
targets with high maximum Health. This Talent should only be picked alongside
Massacre,
as the percent-based damage will be applied to all targets hit.
It does, however, compete with Soul Collector, which greatly improves your survivability.
Memento Mori's damage boost is not good enough to justify
the choice, as Soul Collector will add excellent survivability,
while Mortality will apply more reliable damage
into the fight. It also has terrible synergy with the most versatile Level 13 Talent,
Inevitable End.

talent_pages.title: Level 20 Talents for Malthael
talent_pages.text:
✘︎
Reaper of Souls
(Level 20)
Malthael
Increase the duration of Tormented Souls to 6 seconds, and while Tormented Souls is active, Hero Takedowns refresh its duration.
If 2 or more enemy Heroes are in Tormented Souls' radius, it does not decay.
?
Angel of Death
(Level 20)
Malthael
Last Rites heals for 100% of the damage dealt, and its current and future cooldown reduction bonuses are doubled.
?
Final Curtain
(Level 20)
Malthael
Death Shroud leaves a trail in its wake for 4 seconds, applying Reaper's Mark to enemies in its area.
✓
No One Can Stop Death
(Level 20)
Malthael
Cooldown: 180 seconds
Activate while dead to immediately respawn at the Hall of Storms but increase Malthael's next respawn time by 25%.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Reaper of Souls is a winmore Talent with outstanding potential
against team compositions featuring Murky or The Lost Vikings, who can reliably
be killed to trigger Reaper of Souls' duration increase. Otherwise, you would
be better served by Final Curtain.
Angel of Death provides Malthael with an alternative source of self-healing,
and one that is potentially powerful. If you have been successfully killing
targets through Last Rites only to die shortly after, Angel of Death
may be worth considering, though it is seldom more powerful than Final Curtain.
If you managed to get at least 5 kills with Last Rites, Angel of Death becomes
much more attractive, as it will instantly bring the Ability's cooldown to its
cap of 15 seconds.
Final Curtain significantly improves your ability
to apply Reaper's Mark to
multiple targets, greatly improving your damage over time potential and
self-sustain. The trail created by this Talent also acts as a
zoning tool, and is extremely punishing to opponents who must fight
in enclosed spaces.
No One Can Stop Death is potentially useful to salvage losing matches by
giving you another chance at life. It should be noted that this Talent can be
picked while dead to allow you to revive. This Talent is the standard choice here,
as it can be used in multiple ways, and will be effective in every game.
In Heroes of the Storm, a match can be easily
decided by a kill during the late game. No One Can Stop Death
allows Malthael to trade his life with someone else very often through Last Rites,
which can win the game for your team.
